business_context.ambition: Own the mixed-use home workspace and prove a profitable route from first object to repeat purchase before buying more reach.
business_context.business_model: Founder-led direct-to-consumer home and work accessories

unresolved_inputs: Actual net contribution margin by product and channel
Validated monthly ramp, seasonality and capacity

creative_territory.asset_alt: Fictional FIELDWORK modular desk object on a lived-in dining table shared by work and family life
creative_territory.description: Use real traces of domestic work as the setting, then annotate the product decisions that make a shared surface calmer without pretending life is tidy.
creative_territory.example_execution: A film keeps the camera on one dining table as invoice, lunch, school drawing and late call replace each other. The FIELDWORK object stays, adapts and gathers the day's essential tools. Product annotations explain every material and modular choice.
creative_territory.name: Built for the work of living
creative_territory.platform: Objects designed for the table where invoices, lunch, school drawings and late calls all happen.
creative_territory.validation_test: Test founder authenticity, customer recognition, distinctiveness and whether the territory improves product understanding.

evidence_gaps: Verified revenue by channel, tax basis, returns and discounts
Contribution margin, fulfilment cost and implementation budget
Customer needs, preference, retention and willingness to pay
Competitor positioning, pricing, share and creative activity

evidence_ledger.claim: FIELDWORK receives 600,000 ecommerce sessions per year.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No GA4 export exists for this fictional company.
evidence_ledger.title: Assumed annual ecommerce sessions
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Reconcile an authorised GA4 export to ecommerce platform sessions and orders.

evidence_ledger.claim: FIELDWORK converts 2.0% of ecommerce sessions to orders.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No analytics or order export exists for this fictional company.
evidence_ledger.title: Assumed ecommerce conversion rate
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Agree the conversion denominator and reconcile sessions to completed non-refunded orders.

evidence_ledger.claim: FIELDWORK has a £100 average order value before returns and discounts.
evidence_ledger.limitations: VAT, discounts and returns are not represented.
evidence_ledger.title: Assumed average order value
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Calculate net realised order value from an authorised transaction export.

evidence_ledger.claim: The principal growth constraint is a broad proposition that gives qualified buyers too little reason to choose FIELDWORK.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No customer, funnel or competitor research supports this diagnosis.
evidence_ledger.title: Working constraint hypothesis
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Run founder interviews, proposition testing and a controlled landing-page conversion test.

evidence_ledger.claim: FIELDWORK can build an advantage around objects designed for the overlap between work and home life.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No customer preference or competitor evidence supports ownability.
evidence_ledger.title: Proposed brand advantage
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Test relevance, distinctiveness and willingness to pay with target customers.

evidence_ledger.claim: A proposition-led acquisition, conversion and retention programme is operationally feasible.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No channel economics, media budget, inventory capacity or retention cohorts exist.
evidence_ledger.title: Proposed growth engine
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Obtain channel spend, contribution margin, stock capacity and cohort retention before scale.

evidence_ledger.claim: A staged 12-month validation programme is affordable and resourced.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No cost, owner capacity or dependency plan has been approved.
evidence_ledger.title: Proposed delivery roadmap
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Scope the work, cost each phase and secure named owner commitments.

evidence_ledger.claim: Incremental revenue contributes 32% after returns, fulfilment, payment fees and incremental media.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No product, channel, returns or fulfilment contribution data exists for this fictional company.
evidence_ledger.title: Assumed incremental contribution margin
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Reconcile order-level net revenue and variable costs by product and channel.

evidence_ledger.claim: The business realises 35% to 65% of annualised scenario headroom in the first 12 months.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No implementation plan, seasonality profile or test velocity supports the ramp range.
evidence_ledger.title: Assumed first-year ramp
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Build a monthly implementation plan with test cadence, seasonality and operational capacity.

evidence_ledger.claim: The first 12 months require £85,000 of incremental implementation investment beyond the Growth Blueprint fee.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No suppliers, media plan, production scope or internal time costs have been quoted.
evidence_ledger.title: Assumed implementation investment
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Obtain a costed delivery plan and separate one-off, variable and internal costs.

evidence_ledger.claim: Built for the work of living is an illustrative creative territory for FIELDWORK.
evidence_ledger.limitations: The territory has not been tested with a founder, customer or legal reviewer.
evidence_ledger.title: Creative territory illustration
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Test strategic fit, distinctiveness, comprehension and trademark risk before selection.

channels.role: Prove the proposition and convert qualified demand
Build repeat, cross-sell and referral evidence

channels.gate: Incremental contribution after creative and media cost
channels.role: Scale tested creative and proposition routes
Reach relevant work and design communities

measurement.metrics: Proposition comprehension, qualified click-through, product-page progression
Net conversion, average order value, repeat and referral
Contribution after returns, fulfilment, media and implementation

growth_engine.scale_gate: Increase paid acquisition only after proposition comprehension, net conversion and cohort contribution improve without unacceptable returns or discounting.
growth_engine.thesis: Use the owned site to prove the mixed-use proposition, then use the first object to earn a second purchase before paid media scales the system.

roadmap.decision_gate: Matt selects a proposition test and approves its bounded budget.
roadmap.name: Establish the truth
roadmap.outcome: Verify economics, interview customers and test three proposition routes.

roadmap.decision_gate: Continue only if comprehension and net conversion improve.
roadmap.name: Prove the proposition
roadmap.outcome: Run controlled site, product-story and CRM tests with contribution guardrails.

roadmap.decision_gate: Approve scale only when repeat economics and stock capacity support it.
roadmap.name: Build the engine
roadmap.outcome: Codify winning creative, CRM and referral mechanics and assess capacity.

roadmap.decision_gate: Matt approves any material commercial commitment or client-facing release.
roadmap.name: Scale selectively
roadmap.outcome: Increase investment in validated routes and document what changed commercially.

advantage.statement: FIELDWORK could own the mixed-use surface: modular objects designed for the daily collision of paid work, domestic life and limited space.
advantage.validation_test: Compare this territory with organisation-led and status-led alternatives on relevance, distinctiveness, willingness to pay and unprompted recall.

constraint.falsification_test: Reject this diagnosis if a specific mixed-use proposition does not improve qualified product-page progression and net conversion, or if existing cohorts already show strong second-purchase behaviour.
constraint.statement: FIELDWORK is buying attention for a broad design promise before it has proved why a mixed-use household should choose its first object or return for the second.

recommendations.action: Organise the proposition around the moments when work and home collide, rather than a broad accessories catalogue.
recommendations.name: Own the mixed-use surface
recommendations.trade_off: A narrower promise may reduce broad but low-intent traffic.

recommendations.action: Merchandise each object through a specific domestic work moment, with dimensions, material decisions and usage proof visible before purchase.
recommendations.name: Make usefulness visible
recommendations.trade_off: More proof requires disciplined production and may expose weak claims.

recommendations.action: Build modular add-on, post-purchase and referral tests that reveal whether the first object creates a repeatable customer system.
recommendations.name: Earn the second object
recommendations.trade_off: Near-term reach grows more slowly while economics are validated.

strategy.thesis: Turn the mixed-use surface into a category FIELDWORK can own, then prove that one useful object earns the next purchase before scaling acquisition.
